topic: Instantaneous Rate of Change and the Derivative

outline.topic: Instantaneous Rate of Change and the Derivative

sections.title: The Concept of Average Rate (Prerequisite)
sections.content: Define average rate of change as the slope of a secant line between two points on a curve. Emphasize that this only gives a 'big picture' view, not the specific behavior at a single moment.
sections.example: A cheetah running: Calculating its average speed by dividing the total distance (100m) by the total time (5s) gives 20m/s, but ignores its acceleration/deceleration phases.

sections.title: The Transition to Instantaneous Rate
sections.content: Visualize the 'Zoom-in' effect. As we slide the second point closer and closer to the first, the secant line transforms into a tangent line. Introduce the limit notation: Δt approaches 0.
sections.example: Visual animation: A speedometer on a car showing changing values; as the time interval Δt shrinks from 1 second to 0.001 seconds, the average speed converges to the 'instantaneous' speed.

sections.title: Defining the Derivative
sections.content: Formally define the derivative as the limit of the difference quotient. Represent this graphically as the slope of the tangent line at a specific point x.
sections.example: The formula: f'(x) = lim(h→0) [f(x+h) - f(x)] / h. Visualize this as a slope 'm' that updates dynamically as you move along a parabolic path.

sections.title: Practical Application & Conclusion
sections.content: Summarize that the derivative is the tool used to measure instantaneous change. Reiterate that while average rate looks at the interval, the derivative captures the 'exact' state at a single moment.
sections.example: A drone pilot checking the battery voltage drop. The derivative helps predict the 'instantaneous' rate of power consumption, ensuring the drone lands safely before the battery hits zero.

storyboard.title: The Concept of Average Rate (Prerequisite)
lecture_lines: Average rate is the secant slope.
animations: Show a curved graph of a function in white (#FFFFFF).
Add two points A and B on the curve in yellow (#FFFF00).
Draw a secant line connecting points A and B in light blue (#00FFFF).
Show the calculation for slope: (f(b)-f(a))/(b-a) in white (#FFFFFF).
Flash the secant line to emphasize the average rate.

storyboard.title: The Transition to Instantaneous Rate
animations: Highlight point A on the curve in green (#00FF00).
Bring point B closer to point A along the curve.
Observe the secant line becoming a tangent line.

storyboard.title: Defining the Derivative
animations: Display the limit notation: lim as h goes to 0 in white (#FFFFFF).
Show the difference quotient: (f(x+h)-f(x))/h in light blue (#00FFFF).
Define the derivative f'(x) as the resulting limit in yellow (#FFFF00).

storyboard.title: Practical Application & Conclusion
animations: Show a physical graph (e.g., position vs time) in white (#FFFFFF).
Label the slope of the curve as velocity in green (#00FF00).
Highlight the derivative as the key to rates of change in yellow (#FFFF00).
